Subject Chinese name for "Central Detective Agency",
20 Museum Road.

Made by ____ and ____ Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

None of the three proposed names are agreeable.
As suggested by D.I. Glover in his report dated August 12, 1938, the following characters : 中央私家偵探所 would be the correct designation for the Central Detective Agency and this was agreed to by Mr. Tonkin on August 15, 1938, but from the cards and printed documents used by the Agency, the characters "私家" (Private) were omitted contrary to original arrangement which is certainly misleading.
I suggest that the original name mentioned in D.I. Glover's report be used.
As to the identification cards the correct translation of an employee of the Detective Agency should be "僱員" and not "探員" which would create a wrong impression for a S.M.P. detective.

C.I.
Please note & inform agency formally & also give them to understand that no recognition whatsoever is afforded by the Police.
Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

D. C. (Special Branch)
Attached cards can either be destroyed in their presence or kept in Hdqrs.
DC Crime

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER / 8 DEC. 1938 / CRIME BRANCH）

Information
Jno Robertson
DC (SB)

Mr. Leslie informed accordingly.

D.S.I.

Subject CENTRAL DETECTIVE AGENCY, 20 MUSEUM ROAD.

Made by D.S.I. PRYDE Forwarded by D. I. GLOVER.

Sir,

With regard to the letter from the French Police dated Oct. 25th 1938, referring to an agent of the Central Agency having been shot dead in the French Concession and requesting that this Agency be warned that the activities of their agents would not be tolerated in the French Concession, also with reference to Louza F.I.R. 3562/38, re, an agent of the Central Agency being charged with "Intimidation", Mr. Tonkin, the foreign manager of this Agency, was called to C.B.H.Q. and warned regarding the activities of his agents. It was also explained to Mr. Tonkin that the Identification Cards carried by his agents, contained a lot of unnecessary particulars, which were misleading to the Chinese public, in that, it would lead the public to believe that the owners of these cards were Police Detectives. At that time Mr. Tonkin agreed to call in all these cards and issue new ones which would only bear the name of the agent concerned, his photograph, and a statement to the effect that he was an agent of the Central Agency.

However, on Oct. 28th a letter addressed to the Commissioner of Police, was received from Mr. Tonkin, stating that he had dis-associated himself with this Agency and was returning all the cards issued to the agents. Mr. Tonkin failed to return the cards and could not be located at the time.

先生，

关于法国警方1938年10月25日来信，提及中央社一名特工在法租界被枪杀，并要求警告该社，其特工的活动在法租界将不被容忍；另参照 Louza F.I.R. 3562/38 号案件，涉及中央社一名特工被指控“恐吓”一事，该社外籍经理唐金（Tonkin）先生被召至犯罪科总部，就其特工的活动受到警告。还向唐金先生解释，其特工携带的身份证包含许多不必要的细节，对中国公众具有误导性，因为这会使公众相信这些持证人是警察侦探。当时唐金先生同意收回所有这些卡片，并发行新卡，新卡上仅载有相关特工的姓名、照片以及表明其为中央社特工的声明。

c/o CENTRAL AGENCY,
20, Museum Road,
Shanghai,

23rd November 1938.

Sub Inspector C.J.B.PRYDE,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
185, Foochow Road,
3rd Floor.
Shanghai.

Dear Mr. Pryde,

I am writing to you semi-officially regarding the result of the conversation I had with you in your office recently, in order to give you time to " digest " the following propositions which I wish to suggest.

CHINESE NAME OF CENTRAL AGENCY. I enclose three suggested names In Chinese characters. I do not read Chinese but am advised that the first one marked (1) would seem to be the most suitable for us to adopt. Should you approve of this, we will use nothing else on all our forms and stationery. Of course the foreign name of " Central Agency " will remain unchanged. Do you approve of No.1 or would you be kind enough to suggest something else ?

IDENTIFICATION CARDS FOR OUR MEN. As soon as we have decided on the above, as regards what Chinese characters to use, I have advised the Central Agency to change all their present identification cards. The new identification cards are to only contain the information to the effect that the bearer of the card ( giving his photo, number, name in Chinese and English) signed by myself and the Chinese Director,are in the employ of the Central Agency at No. 20, Museum Road. All the other details on the old cards re reporting to " station " if anything goes wrong, will be eliminated. As soon as the new cards are ready, we propose to let you see them all for record purposes, if you so desire, and keep you posted up to date should any further cards be issued.

M.TONKIN. I do not know where to locate him at present but as he apparently did not keep duplicates of his correspondence with the S.M.P. I am at a loss to know what has done or promised to do and what information is pending from him to you. May I suggest you let me have a rough list of all your requirements or information you were expecting from Tonkin and I will then do my best to get everything straightened out as soon as possible. What I would like to do is to cancel , if at all possible, all Tonkin's papers etc and commence a new record with us - of course I understand that there may be some matters which cannot be cancelled and must be settled right away. If this is the case, will you be kind enough to let me know what you require us to do to get things settled and I will do my best to assist you.

MY POSITION WITH THE CENTRAL AGENCY. As I am employed elsewhere during regular office hours, I am only assisting the Central Agency in my spare time in the capacity as " foreign adviser " I want you to know this so that you will be under no misapprehension as regards my position there. Of course I have been given full powers to act and sign for them.

Please give me a ring sometime when you are ready ( at 13918 or 12670 ) and I will drop around to see you and have a chat with you.

Yours very truly,
[Signature]

July 5, 1938.
Central Agency, Room No.210, 81 Jinkee Road.

With reference to the attached letter dated June 21,
1938 from Mr. C. Tonkin, Central Agency, with an office at
Room 210, 81 Jinkee Road, I have to report that careful en-
quiries go to show that the personnel of this concern lack
the necessary qualifications to operate a private detective
bureau and are otherwise of very doubtful reputation.

The writer of the letter is Mr. Charles Tonkin who
describes himself as the principal partner in the business.
He is a British subject of pure English parentage and was
born in Shanghai in 1887. He is in possession of British
passport No. 89 issued in Peking on January 27, 1923.

Charles Tonkin joined the outdoor staff of the
Asiatic Petroleum Company in or about 1910 and rose to the
position of District Inspector. In 1923 when he was attached
to the Chengchow branch of the company he was dismissed for
general dishonesty involving the systematic embezzlement of
the company's funds, a fact which I have verified in the
course of my enquiries. He came to Shanghai from Peking
in 1923 and for the summer season of 1924 was State Manager
of the Mokanshan Mountain Resort. A testimonial in his
possession, signed by Mr. R.M. White, secretary of the Mokanshan
Summer Resort Association, show that his services were ter-
minated at the close of the 1924 season owing to a change in
the political status of Mokanshan. In 1925 he was associated
with an American Jew named Rosenberg in a so-called Import
and Export firm known as the "Rosenberg China Coy" which had
its offices in the D.K.K. Building 110 Szechuen Road. This
firm, purchased a leather factory opposite Jessfield Park
in which Tonkin claims to have invested $10,000. It
appears that this venture proved a failure for lack of
sufficient capital and the factory closed down in 1926.
Tonkin estimates that his losses through his association

关于附件中1938年6月21日来自仁记路81号210室中央事务所的C.汤金先生的信件，我必须报告说，经过仔细调查表明，该机构的人员缺乏经营私人侦探社所需的资格，且声誉非常可疑。

信函作者是查尔斯·汤金先生，他自称是该业务的主要合伙人。他是纯英国血统的英国臣民，1887年出生于上海。他持有1923年1月27日在北京签发的第89号英国护照。

查尔斯·汤金于1910年左右加入亚细亚火油公司（Asiatic Petroleum Company）的外勤 staff，并晋升至地区督察职位。1923年，当他隶属于该公司郑州分公司时，因涉及系统性挪用公司资金的普遍不诚实行为而被解雇，这一事实在我的调查中已得到核实。他于1923年从北京来到上海，并在1924年夏季担任莫干山度假村的州立经理。他持有的一份由莫干山避暑会秘书R.M.怀特先生签署的证明信显示，由于莫干山政治地位的变化，他的服务在1924年季末终止。1925年，他与一位名叫罗森伯格（Rosenberg）的美籍犹太人合伙经营一家所谓的进出口公司，名为“罗森伯格中国公司”（Rosenberg China Coy），其办公室设在四川路110号大康大楼（D.K.K. Building）。这家公司购买了静安寺路对面的一家皮革厂，汤金声称在其中投资了10,000美元。看来这次冒险因资本不足而失败，工厂于1926年关闭。汤金估计，他通过与罗森伯格的合伙关系造成的损失

page_data.en:
(2)

with Rosenberg amounted in all to $5,500. A well-informed
American citizen of my acquaintance, however, states on good
authority that Tonkin and Rosenberg were in reality engaged
in the illicit export of morphine to the U.S.A. and that their
business venture was simply a "front" to cover up their ac-
tual activities. While the U.S. Authorities appear to have
no record of either Rosenberg or Tonkin, I am convinced as
to the truth of my information and it is a significant fact
that Tonkin's younger brother Mathew Tonkin was arrested in
Hongkong in 1924 for smuggling a quantity of marphine into
the Colony from Europe in concert with a Russian Jew named
Moses L. Samsanovitch. From all accounts, it seems that
the morphine was smuggled into Hongkong inside the tubing of
a shipment of bedsteads of which Mathew Tonkin was the con-
signee. Mathew Tonkin was appropriately charged for this
offence before the Police Court in Hongkong and was sentenced
to seven months' imprisonment, whilst it appears that no
action was taken against Samsanovitch for lack of sufficient
evidence of his complicity. While on the subject of Mathew
Tonkin, it should also be mentioned that he was in some way
implicated in the operation of a Red Pills factory situated
at 20 Tongshan Road in the early part of 1935 (Vide F.I.R.
42/35 Chengtu Road) but no action was taken against him on
the advice of Messrs. Hansons who contended that there was
insufficient evidence to support a charge.

For several years after his business venture with
Rosenberg who incidentally is now in America, Charles Tonkin
does not appear to have been in steady employment. In 1930,
however, he secured a job with Messrs. Jardine and Matheson
as a purser and served in this capacity on the s.s. "Tungwo",
until March 18, 1931 when he was made to resign. He is in
possession of a letter from this company stating that his
services were dispensed with owing to reduction of staff
but confidential enquiries elicit the information that he
was in actual fact dismissed for mismanaging the ship's funds.
page_data.zh:
(2)

总计达5,500美元。然而，我认识的一位消息灵通的美国公民根据可靠消息来源称，汤金和罗森伯格实际上从事的是向美国非法出口吗啡的活动，他们的商业冒险仅仅是一个掩盖其实际活动的“幌子”。虽然美国当局似乎没有罗森伯格或汤金的记录，但我确信我所获信息的真实性，而且一个重要的事实是，汤金的弟弟马修·汤金（Mathew Tonkin）于1924年在香港被捕，罪名是与一名名叫摩西·L·萨姆萨诺维奇（Moses L. Samsanovitch）的俄籍犹太人合谋，将一批吗啡从欧洲走私进殖民地。据各方说法，吗啡似乎是藏在一批床架的铁管中走私进入香港的，马修·汤金是这批货物的收货人。马修·汤金因此罪行在香港裁判司署被适当起诉，并被判处七个月监禁，而似乎由于缺乏足够的证据证明萨姆萨诺维奇的共谋关系，未对其采取任何行动。谈到马修·汤金，还应提及他在1935年初以某种方式牵涉到位于唐山路20号的一家红丸工厂的运营（参见成都路 FIR 42/35），但根据汉森律师事务所（Messrs. Hansons）的建议，未对他采取任何行动，该律所认为没有足够的证据支持指控。

在与罗森伯格（顺便提一下，他现在在美国）进行商业冒险之后的几年里，查尔斯·汤金似乎没有稳定的工作。然而，在1930年，他在怡和洋行（Messrs. Jardine and Matheson）找到了一份事务长（purser）的工作，并在“通和”轮（s.s. "Tungwo"）上担任此职，直到1931年3月18日被迫辞职。他持有该公司的一封信，声明由于裁员而终止了他的服务，但机密调查透露的信息是，他实际上是因为管理船款不当而被解雇的。

page_data.en:
(3)

Latterly he has been associated with a German mining engineer
named Kuscha, who now has an office at 15 Museum Road and
who appears to be a reputable person. In the summer of
1937 he and Kuscha were interested in some mining project
in Anhwei but were compelled to abandon it upon the outbreak
of hostilities.

Tonkin has been a member of the S.V.C. **〔此处转录不清〕** at
different intervals since 1903 and served with this corps
in 1937 for the duration of the hostilities.

Tonkin has established the Central Agency in partnership
with a Chinese named Hatchel Waung alias Waung Chi (汪济)
aged 35, native of Nanking. This individual about a
month ago started a business under the signboard of "Linsen
Trading Coy" in Room No.4, 280 Peking Road for the purpose
of dealing in insecticides priced at 20 cents per tin. Very
little business appears to be done by this so-called company
and a cheque for $40 paid by Waung for the rental of the
room was dishonoured owing to lack of sufficient funds in
his account. Waung claims to have been educated at the
Tsoong Yang Military Academy, Nanking and to have held the
post of Commander-in-Chief of the 18th Division of Chiang
Kai Shek's Army in Foochow until May 1937 when he resigned
and came to Shanghai. It is however very doubtful if this
individual ever held such a prominent position or even that
he served in the Nationalist Army.

Tonkin states that he proposes to operate his agency
on the same lines as Clark's Agency. Among other things,
he hopes in due course to acquire an armoured car for
the purpose of transporting bullion and valuable property
and to man the vehicle with two Russian guards armed with
pistols. He also will engage in the collection of rents
on behalf of Chinese landlords and to carry out enquiries
of a private and confidential nature at the instance of client.

During my visit to the offices of the Central Agency,
page_data.zh:
(3)

近来，他与一位名为库沙（Kuscha）的德国采矿工程师有往来。库沙目前在博物馆路15号设有办公室，似乎是一位声誉良好的人士。1937年夏季，他与库沙对安徽的某项采矿项目感兴趣，但因战事爆发而被迫放弃。

自1903年以来，唐金（Tonkin）断断续续地成为上海义勇队（S.V.C.）**〔此处转录不清〕**的成员，并于1937年在战事持续期间在该队服役。

唐金与一名名叫哈切尔·王（Hatchel Waung），又名王济（Waung Chi）的中国人合伙成立了中央代理行（Central Agency）。王济现年35岁，南京人。此人约一个月前在北京路280号4室以“林森贸易公司”（Linsen Trading Coy）的招牌开始营业，旨在经销每听售价20美分的杀虫剂。这家所谓公司的业务似乎寥寥无几，且王济为支付房间租金所开出的一张40美元支票，因账户资金不足而被退票。王济声称曾就读于南京中央军校，并担任蒋介石军队第十八师师长直至1937年5月，随后辞职来到上海。然而，此人是否真的担任过如此显赫的职位，甚至是否在国民革命军中服役过，都极为可疑。

唐金表示，他打算参照克拉克代理行（Clark's Agency）的模式来经营其代理行。除其他事项外，他希望适时购置一辆装甲车，用于运输金银条及贵重财物，并配备两名持手枪的俄罗斯警卫押运。他还将为中方业主代收租金，并应客户要求开展私密且保密性质的调查。

在我访问中央代理行办公室期间，

page_data.en:
(4)

I observed that there were seven or eight rather suspicious
looking characters sitting in the waiting room. On my
way out I asked Tonkin whether they were members of his
staff and he replied that they were not and explained that
they had called to give information about the transportation
of opium from Hongkew by a gang which had double crossed
them. I sought further particulars about this matter but
Tonkin evaded the question stating that his partner Latchal
Waung was handling the case and that he would let me know
if there was any truth in their information. The appearance
of these individual certainly gave me a rather bad impression
and made me feel that Tonkin was up to some shady business.

Quite apart from the presence of these unsavoury charac-
ters, it became quite evident to me during my interview with
Tonkin that he is more familiar with the ramifications of
opium smuggling than he is with the technique of operating
an enquiry agency on legitimate lines. I consider that he
is by no means a fit and proper man to operate such an agency
and that the Police would be well advised to deny him the
right to handle applications for pistol licences on behalf of
individuals who do wish to come to the Police direct and to
refuse to issue pistol licenses to members of his staff or to
grant him any facilities normally enjoyed by a business of
this kind.

For the moment the Central Agency is being kept
under close surveillance and should it transpire that it is
in fact a blind for opium or narcotic transactions I suggest
that steps be taken to close it down.
page_data.zh:
(4)

我注意到候客室里坐着七八个模样相当可疑的人。离开时，我问唐金这些人是否是他的职员，他回答说不是，并解释说他们是来提供情报的，称有一个团伙在从虹口运输鸦片的过程中背叛了他们。我就此事进一步询问详情，但唐金避而不答，称他的合伙人拉查尔·王（Latchal Waung）正在处理此案，如果他们的信息属实，他会告知我。这些人的外表确实给我留下了相当糟糕的印象，使我觉得唐金正在从事某种见不得光的勾当。

撇开这些令人厌恶的人物在场不谈，在与唐金的谈话中，我清楚地发现，他对鸦片走私的错综复杂网络比他对合法经营调查机构的技术更为熟悉。我认为他绝非经营此类代理行的合适人选，警方最好拒绝他代表那些本愿直接向警方申请的个人办理手枪执照申请的权利，拒绝向其职员发放手枪执照，并拒绝给予他此类行业通常享有的任何便利。

目前，中央代理行正受到严密监视。如果事实证明它确实是鸦片或毒品交易的幌子，我建议采取措施予以取缔。
